title: Opus prefixes every command with 'cd "$PWD" &&', which makes kiln treat read-only commands as unknown and prompt (sed -n, git status)
observed: Model behaviour plus kiln strictness. Every bash call Opus made in this session started 'cd "$PWD" && …'. Because $PWD is an expansion, kiln cannot prove the cd stays in the workspace, so the read-only fast path drops: 'cd "$PWD" && sed -n '1,15p' internal/httpapi/server_test.go' prompted (prompts.log t6c-3), and git status was offered as a rule 'git status *' in several prompts. kiln's bash tool description does not mention cd (internal/tools/bash.go).
expected: Either treat a leading 'cd "$PWD"' (or 'cd .') as the no-op it is, as kiln already does for a cd to the working directory itself, or tell the model in the bash tool description that commands already run in the working directory and need no cd.

fix.note: 04817c4 on branch worktree-agent-ae1e528c60b007fe6 (not merged). Read-only check NOT widened: Claude Code also treats cd with $PWD as not read-only (containsUnquotedExpansion flags $ inside double quotes). Fixed through the bash tool description; a literal cd to a workspace dir was already transparent. Whether models stop adding the prefix is unverified.
